newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraq's Aziz, in Turkey, assails US over oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz, in Turkey, assails US over oil deal.

text.p: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz visited Turkey on Tuesday and told foreign powers to keep out of their mutual affairs.
"Foreign powers should not interfere with our relationship. This is what we want," Aziz told reporters, describing "friendly" Turkey as Iraq's "brother".
He later held talks with Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.
Aziz criticised the United States for its role in delaying an oil-for-food deal signed by the United Nations and Baghdad, which is under U.N. sanctions for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"The American interference in the situation is complicating it, not only against Iraq but also against the interests of Turkey," Aziz said after meeting Ciller.

Before sanctions, Iraq was Turkey's third largest trade partner and top oil supplier and hopes to benefit from limited oil sales through a pipeline running from Iraq's Kerkuk oil fields to a Turkish port under the oil-for-food agreement.
"Nobody is expending more effort to reopen the pipeline than Turkey," Ciller said after meeting Aziz.

Erbakan, who has tried to improve economic ties with Iraq since he came to power four months ago, reiterated Turkey's complaints about the cost of a U.N. trade embargo imposed on Iraq for its role in the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"Our relationship has suffered because of this embargo. It has cost Turkey about $30 billion," Erbakan told reporters.
Erbakan said Turkey aimed to promote peace in northern Iraq and develop trade relations with Baghdad.
But in Baghdad the official Iraqi news agency INA said Iraq had protested to the United Nations against what it termed "violations of Iraq's airspace and territory by Turkish troops".

It quoted a letter from Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali as saying: "The Turkish troops' shelling of Iraq's villages and towns in the north and entering illegally its territory represent a flagrant violation of Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity."
Turkey has periodically sent its forces across the border into northern Iraq in pursuit of Kurdish rebels fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey.
Sahaf urged Ankara to end the mandate of U.S. and allied forces policing a no-fly zone in northern Iraq.

Ankara last month hosted U.S.-sponsored talks between Iraq's warring Kurdish factions, the Kurdistan Democratic Party and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan. Baghdad at the time criticised Turkey for hosting the talks.
